findings.title: `PrismaPromise` and `Prisma` imports appear unused after the `deleteMany` removal
findings.description: The diff removes the only visible uses of `PrismaPromise<Prisma.BatchPayload>` (the `deleteReminderPromise` array). Both names are still imported from `@prisma/client` in the top import block. Unless other uses exist elsewhere in the file (not verifiable from the diff), these imports are dead and will fail lint's unused-import rule. Also, the `Prisma` specifier on line 10 has no trailing comma, unlike its neighbors.

findings.title: `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` calls `prisma` without an import visible in the diff
findings.description: The new body calls `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)`. The hunk does not add a `prisma` import, so it is unverified whether the file already imports `prisma`. If it does not, the module fails to compile or throws at runtime, and the catch block only logs the error. Confirm the import exists.

findings.title: Dropping the `reminder.scheduled` guard changes which reminders get deleted
findings.description: The old code only cancelled reminders where `reminder.scheduled && reminder.referenceId` held. The new code calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder`/`deleteScheduledSMSReminder` for every reminder. For reminders with no `referenceId`, the email helper now hard-deletes the row. For reminders with a `referenceId`, it sets `cancelled: true` and leaves the row. Same pattern in `bookings.tsx` and `workflows.tsx`. This is intentional-looking but a behavior change worth confirming.

findings.title: Outer condition in WorkflowStepContainer no longer covers sender-ID steps
findings.description: The wrapper condition changed from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded`. The `isSenderIdNeeded` variable is now unused in this branch. If any sender-ID-specific markup lived inside the removed wrapper outside the phone block, it is no longer rendered. The diff does not show the full JSX, so this is unverified.
